usage.outputShape: JSON array at body root; each element { ID, OriginAirport, OriginRegion, DestinationAirport, DestinationRegion, Distance, Source }. ID is the route id; use OriginAirport/DestinationAirport for route coverage.
quirks: The /routes endpoint REQUIRES a ?source= query param (e.g. source=united, source=aeroplan). The bare /routes url returns no useful filter set — always pass source.
Response is a very large JSON array (route coverage for the whole program; ~1.4MB for united). No pagination params on /routes; expect a big payload.

Each element is a route-coverage record (origin/destination/distance), NOT live award availability. For actual award seats use the sibling /search and /availability endpoints; use /trips/{availabilityId} for booking detail.
txHash not captured (confirmed:false) though payment settled and 200 returned; cost confirmed $0.01.
usage.guide: Seats.aero route coverage via StableTravel (award/miles data, synchronous, x402 pay-per-call, ~$0.01). Call GET https://stabletravel.dev/api/seats-aero/routes?source=<program> where program is a mileage program slug like united or aeroplan. The response is a large JSON array of route records, each with ID, OriginAirport, DestinationAirport, Distance, and Source. Read it as the set of routes that program covers; it is NOT live award availability. To find actual award seats, use the program's /search and /availability endpoints instead, then /trips/{availabilityId} for segment/booking detail.
